general.temas: The election campaign dominates the front pages, with interventions by Sánchez, Feijóo and Abascal and debates about possible alliances. Also recurring are the shutdown of air traffic in the United States, the assault on the PP candidate in Hernani, Luis de la Fuente’s comments on racism, and the proposal on Ukraine and NATO attributed to the United States. Only ABC highlights the European investigation into contracts for monitoring bracelets for perpetrators of gender-based violence.
general.motivo_crispacion: The campaign features fierce clashes between the PSOE, PP and Vox, with accusations of corruption, criticism of potential alliances and disparaging remarks. The assault on the PP candidate in Hernani and the cancellation of campaign events heighten tensions, as do Otegi’s statements against the PP and Vox. Judicial and political controversies also feature. As a counterpoint, several front pages include sports, cultural and everyday-interest stories, as well as coverage of the technical problem affecting US air traffic.

El País.resumen:
- Sánchez appeals for the pro-European vote against Abascal, while Feijóo seeks support to reach La Moncloa.
- Abascal defends national priority, and Colau contrasts her healthcare proposal with the PP’s model in Andalusia.
- The PSOE is concentrating its efforts on 18 provinces, and a poll suggests the gap with the PP is narrowing.
- Washington attributes the air traffic shutdown to a wiring problem; Zelensky rejects a possible handover of the Donbas in exchange for NATO membership.
- The front page includes an investigation into suspected fraud, the separation of Dani Alves and Joana Sanz, music and recipes.
El País.motivo_populismo: An informative tone predominates, although expressions such as “stop Abascal”, the contrast between healthcare models and the “prodigy entrepreneur” heighten the sense of confrontation or the sensationalist appeal.
El País.sesgo: The selection prioritises the election campaign and its rivalries, with particular attention to the PSOE, PP and Vox. It presents the positions of different parties, although it highlights Abascal’s alliances with far-right leaders and the contrast between healthcare proposals.

El Mundo.resumen:
- Feijóo presents his platform and promises an audit; Sánchez calls for the election result to be respected.
- Otegi calls for mobilisation against the PP and Vox; the PP reports an assault on Jon Echeverría in Hernani.
- The front page links Sánchez to an alleged corruption scheme and covers Junts’ electoral position.
- International coverage highlights cyberwarfare, negotiations over Ukraine and the closure of US airspace.
- It also addresses technological tensions between the US and China, Luis de la Fuente’s comments and the promotion of a film by Los Javis.
El Mundo.motivo_populismo: Confrontational and disparaging expressions predominate, such as “There will be a clean-up”, “democratic thrashing” and “the far-right figure who backs down”, although several headlines retain a predominantly informative tone.
El Mundo.sesgo: The front page devotes considerable space to the electoral confrontation and takes a critical approach to Sánchez, particularly in claiming that he helped revive a corruption scheme. It also highlights verbal attacks between leaders and the assault reported by the PP.

ABC.resumen:
- Police partially cordon off Puerta del Sol over a possible bomb threat.
- The PP cancels its tour of Gipuzkoa after Jon Echeverría is pelted with stones; Feijóo seeks support on the campaign trail.
- A 14-year-old is stabbed outside a secondary school in Madrid.
- Contracts for anti-abuse monitoring bracelets awarded during Montero’s tenure are under investigation, and millions of dollars surface in an investigation in Hungary.
- The front page also covers sports news, US air travel chaos and Leo XIV’s trip to the Peruvian Andes.
ABC.motivo_populismo: Informative headlines predominate, although expressions such as “Black Friday” and “takes your breath away” add drama and emotional emphasis.
ABC.sesgo: The selection gives prominence to security-related incidents and the PP’s activities, alongside an investigation linked to Irene Montero’s tenure. These headlines do not establish an unequivocal ideological orientation.

Público.resumen:
- The front page highlights education cuts, the failure of trilingual education and criticism of the PP and Vox healthcare model.
- On the campaign trail, Sánchez calls on Feijóo to accept the results, while the latter’s relationship with Marcial Dorado resurfaces; other headlines focus on Figaredo and Sánchez’s circle.
- The PSOE prepares for judicial developments and calls for an investigation into payments by the publisher of 'OkDiario' to Koldo’s defence; Aldama alleges an attempted blackmail by Inda.
- The front page addresses the lack of clarity over who should investigate the purchase of a penthouse linked to Ayuso’s government and the potential electoral influence of several content creators.
- The United States rules out a cyberattack as the cause of the air traffic suspension and expects up to 5,000 flight cancellations.
Público.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “the well-heeled boy who didn’t turn out so well”, “perrosanxe”, “litter”, “phantom” and “rights under threat” draw on disparagement, metaphor and emotional language.
Público.sesgo: The selection and wording show an approach that is particularly critical of the PP and Vox, especially on education, healthcare and judicial matters. There are also disparaging or critical headlines about Sánchez’s circle and issues affecting the PSOE.

OKdiario.resumen:
- José Antonio Marina reflects on young people’s happiness; another headline examines why some people look down when talking.
- A hospitality business owner describes the difficulties of keeping a rural bar open; Ana Botín talks about leadership and the weight of her surname.
- Abascal criticises the government over its actions regarding women. A local police officer is shot and wounded in Palma.
- The front page covers Cristiano Ronaldo’s farewell and preparations for Spain v England.
- One story recalls how the first digital image was created in 1957.
OKdiario.motivo_populismo: Confrontational expressions stand out, such as “women are the group that has been cheated the most”, as do alarmist or oversimplifying formulations such as “it is an easy trap to fine you” and “they don’t do it out of shyness”.
OKdiario.sesgo: The selection favours personal-interest content, attention-grabbing statements and sport. In politics, the verb “exposes” casts Abascal’s criticism of the government in a favourable light.

opiniones.comunista:
I see in this campaign a dispute that goes beyond names and slogans: who decides what happens to the wealth we produce, and whom they govern for. The proposal to expand public healthcare points in the right direction, but promising coverage is not enough if services remain subject to the logic of private business. I advocate adequate funding, decent employment and public management, alongside collective ownership of essential resources.

The national priority proposed by Vox pits workers against one another based on their origin while leaving the power of big capital intact. Against that division, I believe in universal rights and collective organising. And in response to the announcement of a deputy premiership for housing, I ask what measures will guarantee affordable homes: changing the organisational chart is not the same as putting housing at the service of those who need it.
opiniones.anarquista:
I see a campaign that asks us to choose who will manage our lives. Some invoke tactical voting; others promise a clean-up or a deputy premiership for housing. I distrust this contest for control: changing who occupies the state does not eliminate the hierarchy that places decisions far from those who bear their consequences.

I am especially concerned about the national priority proposal: making origin a criterion for access to rights pits people with shared needs against one another. And I reject the assault on the PP candidate in Hernani: the freedom to express ideas cannot depend on force.

Against the control exercised by parties and governments, I advocate neighbourhood organisations, mutual aid and direct management of common resources. These are not an excuse to abandon healthcare or housing: they are a way to challenge who makes decisions about them, with equality and individual and collective freedom.
opiniones.liberal:
Today I miss a campaign that talks less about blocs and more about freedom. The promise of a deputy premiership for housing does not guarantee more homes: I would rather reduce barriers to construction, protect property and let competition increase supply. I also want lower taxes and a limited state, capable of funding its essential functions without treating every problem as an excuse to grow.

I reject “national priority” when it means inequality before the law: individual rights should not depend on origin. And the assault on a candidate in Hernani reminds me that political freedom requires security for everyone, whatever their views.

Personal responsibility also matters in politics: those who manage public money must be accountable, and those who promise more spending should explain how they intend to pay for it.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I am concerned that the defence of national sovereignty is being presented as a threat to Europe. Cooperating with our neighbours should not prevent us from deciding whom we admit, how we protect our borders and which needs we prioritise when allocating public resources. National priority deserves democratic debate and legal reform, not a moral veto dictated from behind closed doors.

I am also outraged by the assault in Hernani that led the PP to cancel its tour. Without security to campaign, political freedom becomes an empty promise. I demand protection for all candidates, whatever their views.

Against a campaign of slogans and manoeuvres, I want accountable institutions and a country that defends its communities and traditions. The investigations into contracting and corruption must be resolved without privileges for anyone.
opiniones.centro:
I am concerned that the campaign is becoming a competition in insults. The assault in Hernani is unacceptable: all parties must be able to defend their ideas without intimidation. I also reject the “national priority” proposed by Vox: a democracy must protect equality before the law, not turn rights into a reward reserved for people according to their origin. Defending Europe and its institutions requires more than using its name as a slogan.

The PP’s proposal to create a deputy premiership for housing deserves to be debated on the basis of its potential results, not just its rank. I would focus on increasing supply, facilitating investment and protecting those facing the greatest difficulties, through stable agreements and gradual reforms. And in the face of corruption suspicions, I call for independent investigations and accountability where wrongdoing is proven, without confusing accusations with convictions. Public trust is rebuilt through transparency, not impunity or premature judgments.
